request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite, the durrok, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. A low, barrel-bodied quadruped on four short, thick legs, buried under long, pale, glossy white hair that hangs in heavy, wet-looking ropes to the ground, hiding the body outline so it looks like a soaked haystack. The front end is a blunt, featureless mound of hair, with the head and neck hidden entirely under the hair: eyes, ears, muzzle and horns are all out of sight. Mats of grey-green lichen sit in drifts across the back, shoulders and legs, with loose strands trailing where they slip. Behind, a tail-like fall of white cords hangs to the ground in place of a tail. The legs are short and thick, barely showing under the hair, and stay the same length in every view. Consistent proportions across all facings at one shared scale: one standing animal with the same shoulder height, back height, body bulk and leg length in the side, front and rear views. In side view the body is low and long, its height about 0.6 times its length. In the front view, seen with the blunt hair-covered front end toward the viewer, the body is narrower than the side-view length and exactly as tall as the side view. In the rear view, seen from behind, the fall of white cords and the haunches are exactly as tall as the side view and the front view, with the width changing only as the body turns. Every facing sits well inside the canvas with margin around it, with no facing filling the canvas width.
